name: Saver
brief: A class for exporting a paint object into a specified file, from which to recover the paint data later.
description: ThorVG provides a feature for exporting & importing paint data. The Saver role is to export the paint data to a file. It's useful when you need to save the composed scene or image from a paint object and recreate it later.

The file format is decided by the extension name(i.e. "*.tvg") while the supported formats depend on the TVG packaging environment. If it doesn't support the file format, the save() method returns the `Result::NonSupport` result.
Once you export a paint to the file successfully, you can recreate it using the Picture class.
warnings: This class is not designed for inheritance.

members.name: background
members.brief: Sets the base background content for the saved image.

params.name: paint
params.description: The paint to be drawn as the background image for the saving paint.

members.name: save
members.signature: Result save(Paint* paint, const char* filename, uint32_t quality = 100) noexcept
members.brief: Exports the given `paint` data to the given `path`
description: If the saver module supports any compression mechanism, it will optimize the data size. This might affect the encoding/decoding time in some cases. You can turn off the compression if you wish to optimize for speed.

params.name: paint
params.description: The paint to be saved with all its associated properties.

params.name: filename
params.description: A file name, including the path, where the paint data will be saved.

params.name: quality
params.description: The encoded quality level. @c 0 is the minimum, @c 100 is the maximum value(recommended).

retvals.description: When trying to save a file with an unknown extension or in an unsupported format.
In case an empty paint is to be saved.

notes: Saving can be asynchronous if the assigned thread number is greater than zero. To guarantee the saving is done, call sync() afterwards.

members.name: save
members.signature: Result save(Animation* animation, const char* filename, uint32_t quality = 100, uint32_t fps = 0) noexcept
members.brief: Export the provided animation data to the specified file path.
description: This function exports the given animation data to the provided file path. You can also specify the desired frame rate in frames per second (FPS) by providing the fps parameter.

params.name: animation
params.description: The animation to be saved, including all associated properties.

params.name: filename
params.description: A file name, including the path, where the animation will be saved.

params.name: quality
params.description: The encoded quality level. @c 0 is the minimum, @c 100 is the maximum value(recommended).

params.name: fps
params.description: The desired frames per second (FPS). For example, to encode data at 60 FPS, pass 60. Pass 0 to keep the original frame data.

retvals.description: if there are ongoing resource-saving operations.
if an attempt is made to save the file with an unknown extension or in an unsupported format.
if attempting to save an empty paint.

notes: A higher frames per second (FPS) would result in a larger file size. It is recommended to use the default value.
Saving can be asynchronous if the assigned thread number is greater than zero. To guarantee the saving is done, call sync() afterwards.

members.name: sync
members.brief: Guarantees that the saving task is finished.
description: The behavior of the Saver works on a sync/async basis, depending on the threading setting of the Initializer. Thus, if you wish to have a benefit of it, you must call sync() after the save() in the proper delayed time. Otherwise, you can call sync() immediately.
notes: The asynchronous tasking is dependent on the Saver module implementation.
